title: Worst to First: Sonny Rides Ben Dover All the Way to Buckaroo Bowl III Glory
dek: Two straight last-place finishes, one 13-3 season, and the commissioner finally gets to hand himself the trophy as the 2025 Buckaroo Football League produces its wildest year yet.
body: For two years, Ben Dover was the punchline of the Buckaroo Football League. Sonny finished dead last in 2023 and again in 2024, watching Kaushal hoist Buckaroo Bowls I and II while he ran the league website and, presumably, quietly updated the last-place page with his own name. Then 2025 happened, and the commissioner authored the greatest redemption arc this six-team league has ever seen.

Ben Dover went 13-3 in the regular season, locked up the No. 1 seed, and never really looked back. Here's the part the rest of the league will be bringing up at every draft from now until the heat death of the universe: Sonny's 1,850.8 points for ranked only third in the league. Kaushal and Mekhi both outscored him, which means the commish either mastered the dark art of peaking in the right weeks or has some explaining to do about how this ESPN schedule got made. We're not saying it's an abuse of power. We're just saying the man has admin access and a Boston zip code, and Boston guys are used to things going their way lately.

Speaking of cosmic injustice, Habib deserves a moment of silence. Kaushal led the entire league with 1,973.6 points, more than 120 clear of the champion, and had the record of a coin flip to show for it at 8-8. The two-time champ still earned the No. 3 seed, but the playoffs were not kind: Randy's The fumblers buried the Habibsters 137.1 to 79.96 in a game that was over faster than a Georgia traffic stop. Kaushal settled for third, and the dynasty talk is officially on pause.

That semifinal blowout sent Randy into Buckaroo Bowl III riding the hottest number of the postseason. The No. 2 seed went 9-7 in the regular season and finished with 1,792.1 points, a solid campaign built, as far as we can tell, without anyone ever successfully prying a player loose from his roster. The league saw four trades in 2025, which Randy surely considers four too many on principle. In the big game, though, The fumblers ran out of magic, and Ben Dover took the title 105.1 to 86.48. Two Chicago guys battling for the Bowl, and the one who moved to Boston won. Make of that what you will, Bears fans.

Then there's the saga that will outlive us all. Ramon, aka Brucie, ran Araleasers through Week 8, a stretch that included the season's lowest single-week score, a 61.4 in Week 3. After Week 8 he was kicked out of the league for inactivity, the team was renamed Ramon's Remains, and in its very first game without him it beat Alan 94.76 to 92.02. Read that again: the team got better the moment Brucie stopped touching it. Ramon's Remains finished 5-11 with a league-low 1,523.7 points, and every one of those post-Brucie results sits on his record with an asterisk, a permanent little monument to the most effective benching in league history.

Alan, the league's favorite villain, had his own adventure. Team Pillbert went 5-11, scraped into the No. 6 seed, and somehow climbed to fourth place overall, which is exactly the kind of thing the bad guy does in the second act before getting what's coming to him. Phillibert also has the eternal distinction of being the first victim of a manager-less team, a fact we will be reminding him about roughly once a week in perpetuity.

And finally, poor Kai. Mekhi drafted from basic training, still went 8-8, put up 1,858.2 points (more than the champion!), and dropped the season's biggest single-week number, a monstrous 153.62 in Week 9. The reward for all of that was the No. 4 seed and a trip down the consolation ladder that ended at the very bottom, making Dawgs the 2025 last-place finisher. The guy who probably knows more football than anyone in the league is holding the spoon, the guy who finished last twice is holding the trophy, and the guy who got kicked out won games without lifting a finger. Buckaroo Bowl III, everybody. Never change.
